description: Meloidogyne incognita is a plant-parasitic roundworm that attacks roots of a wide variety of plants, causing large irregular galls. It is one of the most common and economically important root-knot nematodes worldwide.
distribution: Widely spread globally, found in many different soil types, mainly tropical and subtropical regions.

host_range.general: Extremely polyphagous, attacking both monocotyledons and dicotyledons; estimated over 3,000 plant species.

below_ground: Galls on roots, bulbs, and tubers

female.perineal_pattern: Oval to rounded, high dorsal arch, wavy striae, lateral field absent or weakly demarcated

male.head: Not offset, elevated labial disc, usually without lateral lips

life_cycle.description: J2 juveniles hatch from eggs, penetrate root tips, migrate to vascular tissue, form permanent feeding sites (giant cells), molt to adults. Females become globose and lay eggs in gelatinous mass; males leave roots. Life cycle completes in 37 days at 21 °C.
life_cycle.reproduction: Sexually dimorphic; females sedentary, males vermiform

behavior.thermotaxis: Can detect and move along very shallow temperature gradients to find roots
behavior.chemotaxis: Responsive to chemical cues from host roots

cultural_control: Crop rotation with nonhost or resistant varieties
Plant antagonistic crops like Crotalaria spectabilis and Tagetes species
biological_control: Egg-parasitic fungi such as Paecilomyces lilacinus

notes: Causes severe galling and yield loss in many crops
Major economic importance in tropical and subtropical agriculture
